It is celebrated for its unwavering commitment to quality, utilizing fresh, seasonal ingredients to craft an extensive repertoire of refreshments that have become synonymous with Mumbai's street food culture.
Reviewers frequently highlight the establishment's ability to maintain high standards of hygiene and flavor despite the immense daily crowds. The atmosphere is quintessentially Mumbai—a high-energy, casual setting where patrons often enjoy their treats standing on the pavement or from the comfort of their cars, adding a unique drive-in charm to the experience.
• Signature Fruit Creams: The "Sitaphal" (custard apple) cream is universally acclaimed as a must-try masterpiece, featuring a luscious, thick consistency generously laden with fresh fruit chunks.
• Exotic Shakes & Juices: Guests often praise the Mango Milkshake for its rich, creamy texture and the "Triveni"—a sophisticated blend of mango, strawberry, and kiwi juices.
• Savoury Accompaniments: Beyond beverages, the menu boasts popular fusion snacks like the Jain Pizza and the indulgent Cheese Toast, noted for its generous cheese-to-bread ratio.
• Late-Night Accessibility: Operating from the early morning until well past midnight, it serves as a reliable sanctuary for night revelers seeking high-quality refreshments.

featured_reviews.name: Sanoop ks
featured_reviews.review_text:
Haji Ali Juice Centre is one of those places in Mumbai that almost everyone has heard about, and naturally, expectations are quite high before visiting. The menu is extensive, filled with a wide variety of juices, shakes, and desserts that look appealing at first glance. The taste of the items is definitely good—fresh, flavorful, and satisfying to an extent. You can tell that the ingredients are of decent quality and prepared well.

However, beyond that initial impression, nothing truly stands out. There isn’t anything particularly unique or memorable about the flavors that would make you want to come back again and again. It feels like what you get is something you could easily find at many other juice shops across the city.

One of the biggest drawbacks is how overhyped the place feels. Because of its popularity and constant crowd, you go in expecting something exceptional, but the experience turns out to be fairly average. This mismatch between expectation and reality is quite noticeable.

On top of that, the pricing feels a bit on the higher side for what is offered. While the quality is decent, it doesn’t quite justify the cost, making it seem overrated.

Overall, Haji Ali Juice Centre delivers good taste but nothing extraordinary. It’s worth trying once for the experience, but it may not live up to the hype surrounding it.

featured_reviews.name: S P
featured_reviews.review_text: I have been purchasing Raw Pressery juices for over a year and it's been a mostly good experience. However, over the last 1 month (end of May - June), I noticed two problems: (1) When I opened the juice bottles, they had a distinct stink at the rim. It is the kind of smell that lingers after using dirty dish water. In other words, I get the impression their bottles are not being cleaned and prepared under the right hygiene conditions at the processing plant. Reminds me of the roadside stalls where they dunk used utensils and cutlery into buckets of muddy-looking water. It's an awful sour smell that just ruins the whole experience of consuming an apparently fresh, healthy juice. And (2) The Orange juice has an awful after-taste. Almost like crocin or some sort of medication, may be even pesticide, has been crushed into it. I suspect the oranges are not being washed or scrubbed properly before they're juiced. Together, these two reasons have compelled me to stop purchasing Raw Pressery juices. To be sure of the quality, I bought juice bottles from 4 separate locations / businesses in the city. Unfortunately, I encountered the same problem. I complained to one of the business owners and have also shared my experiences with friends and family. The price point of the products is high (or at least not affordable for most / many), and the company is profiting from the idea of consciousness and purity -- for these reasons, it is extremely important that they observe the strictest product quality controls. I have communicated my concerns to the company and hope they take the necessary measures to fulfill their commercial promise of delivering an excellent product.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Stand By Coffee, Worli on a Sunday after a lovely walk at the Coastal Road promenade, but the experience completely spoiled the mood. The café was in a rush hour, which we understood, but the service was extremely slow and unorganized. We ordered a green tea and a toast and sat right in front of the counter. Even after repeatedly reminding the counter boy and the chef—who were right in front of us—nothing was prepared on time. The toast came after 25 minutes, and the green tea arrived 20 minutes later, only when we got frustrated and asked them to either make it immediately or refund us. By then, the toast had already gone cold.

Another disappointing part was that while placing the order, they didn’t inform us that service charge would be added. Only after paying did we notice it on the bill. We didn’t say anything at that moment because who wants to run back for a small amount while trying to enjoy the day—but the experience that followed made it feel unfair.

When we finally gave our feedback, the staff (possibly the owner) responded casually with just a “thanks for the feedback” and showed no concern. Because of the poor service and attitude, we asked them to remove the ₹30 service charge—not for the amount, but because the service truly didn’t justify it.

I don’t recommend visiting this café on Sundays, and based on this experience, I’m unsure about other days too. This visit really ruined what could have been a great end to a beautiful walk.
